courses.name: Understanding AI: Concepts, Ethics, and Societal Impacts
courses.description: Introduces how AI functions and examines bias, inequality, surveillance and societal consequences without requiring coding.

courses.name: AI in Practice: Tools & Problem Solving
courses.description: Uses no-code AI tools to assess practical applications and ethical tradeoffs in fields such as health, education and design.
courses.prerequisites: SI 326 before or concurrently, with C- or better.

courses.name: Coding without Coding
courses.description: Uses AI assistants to create programs without prior programming study, including simulations, text processing and games.

courses.name: Introduction to Information Ethics
courses.description: Applies ethical frameworks to information technology, including privacy, intellectual property, surveillance and generative AI.

courses.name: Privacy, Surveillance, Technology and Society: a multidisciplinary assessment
courses.description: Examines privacy and surveillance across law, computing, media, health and other disciplines.

courses.name: AI and the Law
courses.description: Examines whether existing legal and regulatory approaches address the ethical and policy consequences of AI and machine learning.

courses.name: Applied Generative AI
courses.description: Builds and evaluates applied generative-AI systems in Python using language-model APIs and local models.
courses.prerequisites: Prior SI 345 (previously SI 330) and SI 385 (previously SI 370).

courses.name: Ethics and Information Technology
courses.description: Examines ethical information practices through social technologies, collective knowledge and game design.

courses.name: From the Beginning of Time to AI: A History of Information
Algorithms and Society
courses.description: Examines algorithmic effects on people and communities, including bias, discrimination, fairness, privacy and justice.

courses.name: Applied AI: Machine Learning
courses.description: Implements machine-learning methods in Python, emphasizing supervised learning with introductions to unsupervised, deep and reinforcement learning.
courses.prerequisites: Term-dependent enforced rule: Winter 2026 had no enforced prerequisites. requirements.title: Declaration eligibility
requirements.summary: A declared major, good academic standing and an approving home college are required. The handbook lists Engineering; LSA; Ford Public Policy; Ross Business; Education; Kinesiology; Music, Theatre & Dance; Nursing; Public Health; Stamps Art & Design; and Taubman Architecture. BSI students may take HCAI, but not the other two UMSI minors.

requirements.title: Letter grades and minor GPA
requirements.summary: Each minor course requires a letter grade of C- or higher; the minor GPA must be at least 2.0.

requirements.title: Residential coursework
requirements.summary: All minor coursework must be completed residentially at the University of Michigan; study-abroad and other-institution courses are not eligible.

requirements.title: Major and minor overlap
requirements.summary: UMSI generally permits major/minor overlap, subject to the major and home department rules. Those local rules have not all been inventoried.

requirements.title: BSI-specific overlap
requirements.summary: SI 310 automatically counts toward both BSI and HCAI. Other HCAI courses cannot also fulfill BSI pathway prerequisites or advanced selectives; SI credits still count toward the BSI overall SI-credit requirement.

requirements.title: Two UMSI minors
requirements.summary: HCAI may be combined with either UX or SMAD, with no course double-counting between the two minors. UX and SMAD cannot be paired.

requirements.title: Declaration and release
requirements.summary: Separate declaration and release requests are required. A release request requires completed or current enrollment in all necessary coursework.

requirements.title: Enrollment and priority
requirements.summary: Courses can be taken before declaration when prerequisites and seats permit; declared minors have enrollment priority. The course-specific registration guide linked from this handbook was unavailable at review.

requirements.title: Renumbered courses
requirements.summary: UMSI accepts both the previous and current names/numbers toward minor progress. The handbook identifies SI 310 as formerly SI 302 and SI 346 as formerly the SI 311 AI and the Law topic.

requirements.title: Variable-credit choices
requirements.summary: PHIL 340 is listed at 2–4 credits and COMM 349 at 3–4. Neither is assigned a guessed fixed amount; actual elected credits must meet the elective minimum.

requirements.title: SI 376 prerequisite relationship
requirements.summary: The handbook identifies SI 326 as a corequisite for SI 376. The current course table permits SI 326 before or alongside SI 376, with C- or better.

requirements.title: Current credits versus historical course count
requirements.summary: The May 2025 launch announcement described three electives. The current handbook instead requires at least nine elective credits and includes 1.5-credit choices; the historical count is not applied to the current inventory.
